name: Ren Jinsheng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2007-2026)
forbes_bio: Ren is the founder and chairman of Simcere Pharmaceutical Group, a pharmaceuticals supplier. .
Simcere has research development centers in Nanjing, Shanghai and Boston.
Ren holds an undergraduate degree in traditional Chinese pharmacology from the Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine.
He also holds a master's degree in business administration from the Nanjing Normal University.

name: Pawan Munjal
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun India (2016-2019)
forbes_bio: Pawan Munjal is the chairman and managing director of Hero MotoCorp,the world's largest producer of two-wheelers by volume having sold more than 120 million units to date.
He inherited a stake in the Hero group after his father Brijmohan Lall Munjal, who cofounded the enterprise with his brothers, died in 2015 at age 92.
A former partner of Honda, Hero MotoCorp parted ways with the Japanese company in 2011. Since then Pawan has led a global expansion with factories in Colombia and Bangladesh.
The group's renewable energy arm, Hero Future Energies, along with U.S. private equity firm KKR, is investing $450 million in expanding capacity.
forbes_facts: In 2022, Hero launched Vida, its first electric scooter.
In 2023, the Delhi High Court stayed a federal investigation into allegations that he took money out of the country illegally. He's denied any wrongdoing.

name: Weng Xianding
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Weng is the majority shareholder of Shenzhen New Industries Biomedical Engineering, a supplier of clinical instruments.
Weng was the first person to be appointed as representative of China's securities watchdog in the city of Shenzhen back in 1992.
The company was founded in 1995 and is based in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen.

name: Edir Macedo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Evangelical bishop Edir Macedo is the owner of Record, the second-largest broadcasting company in Brazil.
Macedo founded the Universal Church of the Kingdom of God in 1977, a neo-Pentecostal religious denomination which now has branches in over 100 countries.
One of the richest religious leaders in the world, Macedo also owns a majority stake in the private Brazilian bank Banco Digimais.
Macedo preaches "prosperity theology," which is the belief that the faithful will be rewarded with material wealth.
In 1992, Macedo spent 11 days in jail on accusations of charlatanism, an event that features prominently in his self-financed documentary "Nothing to Lose."
forbes_facts: In 2014 Macedo inaugurated a replica of Solomon's Temple in Sao Paulo, which seats 10,000 and is twice the height of Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer statue.

name: Su Hua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2019-2022); Hurun China U40 (2019-2022); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Su Hua served as chairman of video-sharing and live-streaming platform Kuaishou Technology until 2023. It was first set up in 2011 as a GIF-maker app.
The company went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2021.
Its pre-IPO investors included funds managed by Fidelity and BlackRock.
Su, a native of Hunan province, was reportedly born in a village that didn't have electricity until 1998.
Before founding Kuaishou, Su worked as a programmer at Baidu and Google.

name: Zeng Chaoyi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025)
forbes_bio: Zeng Chaoyi is a director of Tianshan Aluminum Group, a Chinese supplier of aluminum products.
Tianshan's shares trade at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange; it's headquartered in Xinjiang.
Shimge Pump Industry Group acquired Tianshan Aluminum Group in 2020 in a backdoor listing and changed its name to Tianshan Aluminum Group.
Brother Zeng Chaoyi's brother Zeng Chaolin is Tianshan's chairman and also a billionaire.

name: Ke Xiping
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026)
forbes_bio: Ke Xiping chairs Xiamen Hengxing Group, which has interests in real estate and minerals.
Raised in Fujian Province, Ke Xiping started out in business in the construction materials trade.
Ke's philanthropic donations exceed $30 million.

name: Gloria Joseph
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Gloria Joseph is the ex-wife of George Joseph, the billionaire founder of Los Angeles-based insurance company Mercury General Corporation.
She owns a 17% stake in Mercury, which she received when the couple divorced in 1985.
The couple married in 1946 after George served in the Air Force during World War II.
When George founded Mercury in 1961, Gloria was named vice president, and she served in that role until the couple divorced. She continued to sit on the company's board until 2003.

name: Niraj Shah
sec_insider_companies: Wayfair Inc. (W) - Chief Executive Officer; Nextdoor Holdings, Inc. (NXDR) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2022); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Wikidata (2021); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Niraj Shah is cofounder and CEO of online home goods retailer Wayfair.
He started the business in 2002 with Steve Conine, who is also a billionaire. The two met as high school students at a program at Cornell University.
Shah and Conine ended up living in the same dorm their freshman year at Cornell and became good friends.
Wayfair, which now offers more than 18 million products, generated $14 billion in net revenue in 2020, up 55% from the previous year.
Shah joined the board of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston in 2017.
forbes_facts: In their final semester of college, Conine and Shah both enrolled in a class on entrepreneurism, which sparked a business plan that turned into their first company.
The duo started Wayfair in a spare bedroom of Conine's house. They soon operated 250 websites selling everything from barstools to birdhouses

name: Takaya Awata
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Takaya Awata is president and CEO of Tokyo-listed Toridoll Holdings, Japan's largest operator of udon noodle  restaurants.
Awata opened his first yakitori grilled-chicken restaurant in 1985, after dropping out of the Kobe City University of Foreign Studies.
Toridoll has over 2,000 restaurants in Japan, China, Singapore, Europe. and the U.S.
In 2021, the firm listed its Tam Jai International, an operator of Chinese noodle restaurants that it acquired in 2018, on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange but took it private in August 2025.
The company posted $1.9 billion in revenue in the fiscal year through March 2025, a 16% jump from the previous year.
forbes_facts: In February 2025, Toridoll proposed delisting Tam Jai to make it a wholly-owned subsidiary.

name: Yuri Karptsov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Yuri Karptsov is a cofounder of DNS Retail, Russia's largest chain of consumer electronic products.
Along with Dmitry Alexeyev, a fellow billionaire, Karptsov started with a small store in 1998 in Vladivostok, a port city east of Moscow.
The pair opened its second location in 2005 and have expanded to more than 2,700 stores and 39,000 employees.
The company also has interests in property development and information technology (IT).

name: Michael Andlauer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Michael Andlauer has spent more than three decades running Canadian logistics companies focused on healthcare. He founded Andlauer Transportation Services in 1991 and Associated Logistics Solutions in 1994.
In 2019, he merged several healthcare supply-chain businesses into Andlauer Healthcare Group. It went public on the Toronto Stock Exchange that same year.
In 2004, he took over as majority owner of the AHL's Hamilton Bulldogs and oversaw the club's 2007 Calder Cup victory.
He bought a minority stake in the Montreal Canadiens NHL team in 2009 and served as the team's alternate governor until 2023, when he sold his share of the team.
Andlauer led a group that purchased 90% of the Ottawa Senators in 2023 at a $950 million valuation.

name: Hermanto Tanoko
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Hermanto Tanoko and his brother Wijono control Avia Avian, reportedly Indonesia's second- largest domestic paints company.
The company was founded in 1978 by their father Soetikno Tanoko.
The brothers took it public in 2021 and Hermanto serves as President Commissioner.
Hermanto has also been building his own business empire Tancorp with interests in manufacturing, retail, logistics and property.
Lightweight Brick Manufacturer Superior Prima Sukses, where he owns a stake, went public in 2024 in a deal that values it at $100 million.

name: Hu Kun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2021-2022); Hurun China (2011-2021)
forbes_bio: Hu Kun chairs Shenzhen-listed Contec Medical Systems, a supplier of medical instruments.
Contec went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in August 2020.
More than 70% of Contec's revenue comes from overseas.
